Article 14

1. Prevention of violations of Children's rights shall be implemented by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph I]) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Prevention based on partnership patterns with the Community, private sector, non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Child Protection.
3. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. increasing Children's productivity;
b. developing Children's self-potential;
c. preventing pregnancy at a young age;
d. reducing maternal and infant mortality rates; and
e. preventing the occurrence of domestic Violence.
4. Establishment of a working network as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, includes working partners of the Regional Government in the implementation of Prevention of rights violations in the form of family partners.
5. Further provisions regarding Prevention of violations of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated in Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to carry out efforts for the Prevention of Violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (3) letter e and paragraph (4) letter i in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-Violence values toward Women and Children; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the empowerment of Women and the Protection of Children victims of Violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for victims by involving Community elements; and
b. encouraging Community awareness of the importance of protection for victims of Violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gunung Mas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Community is individuals, community groups, including parents and families.

10. Prevention is all efforts to eliminate all risks and adverse impacts of violence against Women and Children.
11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
12. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as FPK2PA, is a coordination forum for handling victims of Violence against Women and Children whose implementation is tiered at the regency and sub-district levels.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

Paragraph 2

FPK2PA

Article 27

1. In order to protect and guarantee the rights of Women and Children from acts of Violence, FPK2PA shall be established.
2. FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of:
a. Regional FPK2PA;
b. sub-district FPK2PA; and
c. village/ward FPK2PA.
3. The establishment of Regional FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a shall be stipulated by the Regent.
4. The establishment of sub-district FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b shall be stipulated by the sub-district head.
5. The establishment of village/ward FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be stipulated by the village/ward head.
6. Further provisions regarding FPK2PA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 31

1. The Regent is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training;
d. monitoring and evaluation; and
e. reporting.
4. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children in accordance with standard norms, procedures and criteria implemented by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
5. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
6. In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection must report periodically to the Regent.
7. In the case of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus, the Community, agencies and/or related institutional organizations.

CHAPTER III

CHILD PROTECTION

Part One

General

Article 19

1. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children, the Regional Government must carry out cross-sectoral coordination with related institutions.
2. In the implementation of coordination for the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall establish a coordination team for the Protection of Women and Children.
3. In the coordination forum activities as referred to in paragraph (2), the coordination team for the Protection of Women and Children shall have the duties to:
a. prepare the necessary materials related to the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and
b. convey the results, obstacles, and solutions undertaken to overcome obstacles in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
4. The coordination forum as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted periodically, at least 2 (two) times in 1 (one) year.

REPORTING

Article 33

1. Reporting of evaluation results as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (5) shall serve as material for the Regent's consideration in making policy decisions on the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. Reports on the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year and at any time when necessary.

Article 2

Protection of Women and Children is organized based on the principles of:
a. respect, fulfillment, protection, promotion, and enforcement of rights; and
b. legal certainty.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

Prevention of Violence Against Women and Children

Article 14

1. Prevention of violations of Children's rights shall be implemented by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph I]) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Prevention based on partnership patterns with the Community, private sector, non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Child Protection.

a. increasing Children's productivity;
b. developing Children's self-potential;
c. preventing pregnancy at a young age;

e. preventing the occurrence of domestic Violence.

a. prepare the necessary materials related to the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and

1. Reporting of evaluation results as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (5) shall serve as material for the Regent's consideration in making policy decisions on the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. Reports on the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year and at any time when necessary.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Community is individuals, community groups, including parents and families.

10. Prevention is all efforts to eliminate all risks and adverse impacts of violence against Women and Children.
11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
12. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as FPK2PA, is a coordination forum for handling victims of Violence against Women and Children whose implementation is tiered at the regency and sub-district levels.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to carry out efforts for the Prevention of Violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (3) letter e and paragraph (4) letter i in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-Violence values toward Women and Children; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the empowerment of Women and the Protection of Children victims of Violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for victims by involving Community elements; and
b. encouraging Community awareness of the importance of protection for victims of Violence.

Article 14

1. Prevention of violations of Children's rights shall be implemented by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph I]) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Prevention based on partnership patterns with the Community, private sector, non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Child Protection.
3. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. increasing Children's productivity;
b. developing Children's self-potential;
c. preventing pregnancy at a young age;
d. reducing maternal and infant mortality rates; and
e. preventing the occurrence of domestic Violence.
4. Establishment of a working network as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, includes working partners of the Regional Government in the implementation of Prevention of rights violations in the form of family partners.
5. Further provisions regarding Prevention of violations of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated in Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 29

a. prevention of marriage at the age of Children;
b. bringing Women closer to health services; and
c. strengthening family resilience.

Article 2

Protection of Women and Children is organized based on the principles of:
a. respect, fulfillment, protection, promotion, and enforcement of rights; and
b. legal certainty.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

a. increasing Children's productivity;
b. developing Children's self-potential;

e. preventing the occurrence of domestic Violence.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to carry out efforts for the Prevention of Violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (3) letter e and paragraph (4) letter i in the form of:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gunung Mas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Community is individuals, community groups, including parents and families.

10. Prevention is all efforts to eliminate all risks and adverse impacts of violence against Women and Children.
11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
12. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as FPK2PA, is a coordination forum for handling victims of Violence against Women and Children whose implementation is tiered at the regency and sub-district levels.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

Article 19

1. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children, the Regional Government must carry out cross-sectoral coordination with related institutions.
2. In the implementation of coordination for the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall establish a coordination team for the Protection of Women and Children.
3. In the coordination forum activities as referred to in paragraph (2), the coordination team for the Protection of Women and Children shall have the duties to:
a. prepare the necessary materials related to the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and
b. convey the results, obstacles, and solutions undertaken to overcome obstacles in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
4. The coordination forum as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted periodically, at least 2 (two) times in 1 (one) year.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 31

1. The Regent is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training;
d. monitoring and evaluation; and
e. reporting.

6. In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection must report periodically to the Regent.
7. In the case of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus, the Community, agencies and/or related institutional organizations.

Article 14

1. Prevention of violations of Children's rights shall be implemented by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph I]) shall be implemented by:

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

CHAPTER II

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 19

1. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children, the Regional Government must carry out cross-sectoral coordination with related institutions.
2. In the implementation of coordination for the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall establish a coordination team for the Protection of Women and Children.
3. In the coordination forum activities as referred to in paragraph (2), the coordination team for the Protection of Women and Children shall have the duties to:

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gunung Mas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Community is individuals, community groups, including parents and families.

10. Prevention is all efforts to eliminate all risks and adverse impacts of violence against Women and Children.
11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
12. Forum for Handling Victims of Violence Against Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as FPK2PA, is a coordination forum for handling victims of Violence against Women and Children whose implementation is tiered at the regency and sub-district levels.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

CHAPTER VIII

EVALUATION

Article 32

1. Evaluation of the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted based on documents of service implementation, empowerment, Prevention, fulfillment and monitoring results of the administration of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include evaluation of process, impact and results.
4. The results of evaluation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall constitute material for the Regional Apparatus to prepare a report which is subsequently submitted to the Regent.
5. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be implemented at least 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year.
6. Further provisions regarding evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to carry out efforts for the Prevention of Violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (3) letter e and paragraph (4) letter i in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-Violence values toward Women and Children; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the empowerment of Women and the Protection of Children victims of Violence.
2. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility to provide and organize services for victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for victims by involving Community elements; and
b. encouraging Community awareness of the importance of protection for victims of Violence.

Article 14

1. Prevention of violations of Children's rights shall be implemented by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph I]) shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a working network;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Prevention based on partnership patterns with the Community, private sector, non-governmental organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to Child Protection.
3. Prevention of violations of Children's rights implemented by the Community as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by:
a. increasing Children's productivity;
b. developing Children's self-potential;
c. preventing pregnancy at a young age;
d. reducing maternal and infant mortality rates; and
e. preventing the occurrence of domestic Violence.
4. Establishment of a working network as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a, includes working partners of the Regional Government in the implementation of Prevention of rights violations in the form of family partners.
5. Further provisions regarding Prevention of violations of Children's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated in Regent Regulation.

11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.

13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gunung Mas Regency.

3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.

13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination, and acts of Violence, including trafficking in persons established by the government or community-based.
14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gunung Mas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Gunung Mas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
6. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination.
7. Woman is a person who is female.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
9. Community is individuals, community groups, including parents and families.

10. Prevention is all efforts to eliminate all risks and adverse impacts of violence against Women and Children.
11. Violence is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.

13. 14. Child-Friendly Village/Sub-District, hereinafter abbreviated as K/DRA, is the development of a village/sub-district area that unites the commitment and resources of the village/sub-district government involving the Community and business world located in the village/sub-district in order to promote, protect, fulfill and respect children's rights, which are planned consciously and sustainably.

CHAPTER IX

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

CHAPTER VII

Article 31

1. The Regent is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training;
d. monitoring and evaluation; and
e. reporting.
4. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children in accordance with standard norms, procedures and criteria implemented by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
5. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
6. In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection must report periodically to the Regent.
7. In the case of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus, the Community, agencies and/or related institutional organizations.

I. GENERAL

Children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development, participation and the right to protection from acts of Violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise, Women who play a role as mothers who give birth to children who are healthy, strong, resilient, noble in character, potential and of quality. Through the role of Women in the family, Community and state, resilient generations will be born who will continue the nation's ideals.
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, particularly Article 27 paragraph (1) which states that "All citizens shall have equal status in law and government and must uphold the law and government without exception". Although the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has guaranteed equal status for every citizen, to date Women and Children still experience various obstacles in obtaining their rights in almost all fields.

On the other hand, Women have special needs compared to men, so that in accordance with their nature, in certain conditions the Regional Government must be able to guarantee that their rights are fulfilled in accordance with those needs. Whereas children, they are a trust and gift from God Almighty, in whom is inherent the dignity and worth of a complete human being. Considering the position and expectations for children as the potential and future of the nation, children deserve attention from all parties so that children can grow and develop normally and be protected from wrong treatment and actions, Violence, discrimination that will damage the development of children both physically, mentally and socially. For this reason, children need to be given the widest possible opportunity to grow and develop optimally, both physically, mentally, socially and with noble character.

Starting from this matter, a regulation is needed that serves as a guide for all parties, especially the Regional Government in ensuring the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children in Gunung Mas Regency in accordance with the authority possessed as contained in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government, as well as other laws and regulations that regulate the Protection of Women and Children.

5. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (4) shall be implemented at least 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year.
6. Further provisions regarding evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 31

1. The Regent is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the Protection of Women and Children.
2. The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
3. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training;
d. monitoring and evaluation; and
e. reporting.
4. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) to realize the objectives of the Protection of Women and Children in accordance with standard norms, procedures and criteria implemented by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
5. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
6. In implementing guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection must report periodically to the Regent.
7. In the case of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus, the Community, agencies and/or related institutional organizations.
